note: Custom View Filters registers three Views filter handlers on node_field_data via hook_views_data_alter(): custom_az_filter (Views field custom_az_filter), node_granular_date_filter (field nodes_granular_dates), and date_range_picker_filter (field date_range_picker). No settings form, no configure route (configure=null), no permissions, no config schema, no plugin type of its own. All persistent state lives in a View config entity's filter handler options (plugin_id + the field's machine name in az_field_name / granular_field_name). Medium introspection reads back which handler a live View uses; hard execution adds the custom_az_filter handler to a live View and verifies it against the saved views.view config.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib module custom_view_filters adds ready-made filters to Views. Name the three Views filter handler plugin ids it provides and, in one line each, what they filter by.
evals.expected_output: It registers three FilterPluginBase handlers on node_field_data (group 'Custom View Filters'): custom_az_filter (first letter of the first/second word of a text field), node_granular_date_filter (by year and/or month of a date field), and date_range_picker_filter (a since/until date range).

evals.prompt: Using custom_view_filters, how do I tell each filter which field to act on, and which special/built-in field names are supported? There is no field picker.
evals.expected_output: You type the field's machine name into the filter's options: az_field_name for the AZ filter, granular_field_name for the granular-date and date-range filters (e.g. field_build_date). Special names: 'title' for the AZ filter, and 'created' / 'changed' for the date filters, which query node_field_data directly.

evals.prompt: With custom_view_filters, can these filters be exposed to site visitors, and how would I render the exposed control directly in a Views Twig template rather than the default exposed form block?
evals.expected_output: Yes; each filter works as an admin (non-exposed) or exposed filter. Because each exposed widget is a real form element keyed by the filter's exposed identifier, you can print it in a Views template, e.g. {{ form.custom_az_filter }}, {{ form.nodes_granular_dates }}, or {{ form.date_range_picker }}.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a View with machine name cvf_known_view that uses one of the custom_view_filters filters. Inspect the live View configuration and state the module's filter handler plugin id it uses and the field machine name that filter targets.
evals.expected_output: cvf_known_view's default display has a filter with plugin_id node_granular_date_filter targeting granular_field_name 'created' (Views field nodes_granular_dates on node_field_data).

evals.prompt: On this site the View cvf_range_view uses the custom_view_filters date-range picker. Inspect the live View config and report which field machine name its date_range_picker_filter targets.
evals.expected_output: cvf_range_view's default display has a filter with plugin_id date_range_picker_filter whose granular_field_name is field_cvf_when.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a View with machine name cvf_task_view (base table node_field_data) that currently has no custom_view_filters filter. Using the custom_view_filters module, add its Custom AZ filter (handler plugin id custom_az_filter) to the view's default display as a non-exposed filter targeting the node title (az_field_name = 'title'). Save the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: views.view.cvf_task_view default display display_options.filters gains an entry with plugin_id 'custom_az_filter', table 'node_field_data', and az_field_name 'title'.

evals.prompt: The site has a View named cvf_task2_view listing content. Using custom_view_filters, add the year/month 'granular date' filter (handler plugin id node_granular_date_filter) to its default display so it filters on the node's created date (granular_field_name = 'created'). Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: views.view.cvf_task2_view default display display_options.filters gains an entry with plugin_id 'node_granular_date_filter' and granular_field_name 'created'.
